title: Stop closes the prompt's task as a provisional host close; git-side work anchors task records
context: hunch task stats on 2026-09-15: 107 local tasks in 7 days, 7 graph records. Causes measured from the ledger: tasks left open by the agent never became records even with saves and passed checks; edits made through Bash/python patch scripts, rebases and release commits never fired the pre-edit hook, so records had no file anchors for them; each follow-up prompt opened its own task. The earlier rule 'Stop does not close an unfinished report' protected against another hook continuing the turn; reopen-on-observation keeps that safety while making the ledger and the graph truthful without user or agent cooperation (David: 'the user doesn't have to touch anything').
decision: The lifecycle Stop hook closes the prompt's task itself (closed_by: "host") and persists its graph record through persistTaskRecord, so a task with observations becomes memory without the agent calling hunch_task finish. The close is provisional: appendEvent reopens a host-closed task on the next observation (a continued turn after another hook's block, or a verify/rule run after Stop), the following Stop closes it again and refreshes the record (idempotent on report hash), and an explicit agent finish with any outcome overrides a host close and is final. Pending verification keeps the task open. Verification and rule evaluation accept a host-closed task. Task records additionally anchor to files git saw change while the task was open: commits authored by the configured git user whose commit time falls in [started_at-1s, finished_at+1s] (merges excluded, 50 commits max) and working-tree changes whose mtime falls in [started_at, finished_at+1s]; .hunch, .hunch-cache and .git paths and deletions are excluded; report-derived files come first under the 64-file cap. Empty tasks remain ledger-only.
consequences: hunch task list shows completed for every ended turn; closed_by distinguishes host from agent closes
Records may refresh after a continuation; consumers must treat a task record as the latest revision of that task
gitTouchedFiles runs git twice per persist (3 s timeout each, fail-open)
Tests: test/task-report-hook.test.ts host-close/reopen/override; test/task-record.test.ts git-touched files
